title: An ordered dictionary
description:
Build a dictionary from words to whole numbers that keeps its keys **sorted** and answers order questions: the nearest keys, the rank of a key, the k-th key, and the count and **sum** of every key in a range, all in O(log n). Underneath is your own **balanced binary search tree** (an AVL tree is the natural choice) in which every node also stores the **size** and the **sum of values** of its subtree.

```
set pear 40
set apple 10
set fig 25
set banana 20
range b g
rank fig
nth 1
floor grape
ceil grape
del apple
min
size
```

prints

```
added pear
added apple
added fig
added banana
2 keys, sum 45: banana=20, fig=25
2
apple = 10
fig = 25
pear = 40
deleted apple
banana = 20
3
```

Keys are single words, compared the way `std::string` compares them. Values are whole numbers from −1000000000000 to 1000000000000.

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `set <key> <value>` | `added <key>` or `updated <key>` |
| `get <key>` | the value, or `not found` |
| `del <key>` | `deleted <key>`, or `not found` |
| `min`, `max` | `<key> = <value>`, or `empty` |
| `floor <word>` | the largest key `<=` the word as `<key> = <value>`, or `none` |
| `ceil <word>` | the smallest key `>=` the word, or `none` |
| `rank <word>` | how many keys are smaller than the word |
| `nth <i>` | the i-th smallest key, counting from 1, as `<key> = <value>`; `error: there is no key number <i>` if `i` is not from 1 to the size |
| `range <lo> <hi>` | `<c> keys, sum <s>: <k1>=<v1>, <k2>=<v2>, ...` for the keys in [lo, hi] in order; `1 key, ...` for one; `0 keys` for none (also when lo > hi) |
| `count <lo> <hi>` | `<c> keys, sum <s>` for the same range, **without** listing them (this one must be O(log n)) |
| `size` | the number of keys |
| `bulk <prefix> <n>` | sets the keys `<prefix>000001` to `<prefix><n as 6 digits>` to the values 1 to n, in that (sorted) order; `n` is from 1 to 100000. Prints `bulk: <a> added, <u> updated` |
| `check` | `balanced` if the tree's height is at most 2·log₂(n + 1) (true for AVL and red-black trees; the empty tree counts as height −1), otherwise `not balanced (height <h>)` |

Mistakes print `error: unknown command '<word>'`, `error: usage: <usage>` (written as in the first column, for example `range <lo> <hi>`), `error: the value must be a whole number from -1000000000000 to 1000000000000`, or `error: n must be from 1 to 100000`. Blank lines are ignored.
hints: Give the node an `update` that recomputes height, size **and** sum from its children, and call it wherever heights are recomputed: after inserting, deleting and inside both rotations. Then the augmented fields can never fall out of date.

`count lo hi` is "number and sum of keys `<= hi`" minus "number and sum of keys `< lo`". Each is one walk from the root: whenever you go right past a node, add its left subtree's size and sum plus the node itself.
requirements: Write the balanced tree yourself: no `std::map`, `std::set` or sorting of all the keys.
Each node stores its subtree's size and sum, kept correct through every insertion, deletion and rotation.
`rank`, `nth`, `floor`, `ceil` and `count` are O(log n): they walk one or two paths using the stored sizes and sums. `range` is O(log n + k) for k keys listed.
Separate the tree class from the command parsing.
stretch: Add `sumtop <k>` (the sum of the k largest values, not keys), which needs a second tree ordered by value, and `undo`, which reverts the last change by keeping the tree **persistent**: each change copies only the O(log n) nodes on its path and shares the rest with the previous version.
